question: When machines were expected to replace human translators and interpreters, what actually happened to the people doing that work, and which parts of the job stay with people and for how long?

issues.note: Hard cut from the bright 1954 computer hall to the drab 1966 office. The on-screen caption carries the jump, but the change of look and place is abrupt.

The split-screen wipe (1966 postediting beside today) is busy. Right after it, the cut to a wide empty office shows a different room from the monitor close-ups, and the narration 'the change shows up in the...' has no matching image.
Nuremberg 1945 and today are shown side by side, then the picture drops to an empty video-call room. The narration 'And the next ten years?' is carried by a static room with no new visual.
The same monitor close-up stays on screen across R12.1 to R12.5, about 20 s, with only the caption changing.
The typewriter close-up is held for R11.4 to R11.8 with little movement while the narration continues.
The monitor shot is reused for many seconds (R13.7, R14.1, R14.2), then again at R15.4 to R15.8, so it begins to feel repetitive.
